examDifficulty.heading: Is the Tableau Consultant Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Tableau Consultant exam is moderately difficult. It blends technical Tableau product knowledge with consulting and advisory competencies, so strong product skills alone are not enough — you also need experience translating business requirements into Tableau solutions.
bullets: 45 questions in 90 minutes — roughly two minutes per question, which gives adequate time for scenario analysis.
~70% passing score — you need approximately 32 correct answers out of 45 to pass.
Consulting scenarios dominate — questions describe client requirements and ask you to recommend the best Tableau approach, not just identify a feature.
Implementation experience is essential — candidates with real project experience advising clients on Tableau deployments perform significantly better.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Book when you have completed at least one Tableau implementation project and can confidently recommend data source strategies, deployment models, and adoption approaches.

examFormat.heading: Tableau Consultant Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Scenario questions describe a client requirement and ask you to recommend the best Tableau approach — data source strategy, deployment model, or visualization technique.
bestWayToPass: Requirements mapping: Practice translating business questions into Tableau solution designs covering data sources, visualizations, and deployment architecture.
Live vs. Extract trade-offs: Know when to recommend each connection type based on data freshness needs, query performance, and infrastructure constraints.
Tableau Prep knowledge: Understand when to preprocess data in Prep Builder versus using Desktop calculated fields or database-side transformations.
Adoption strategy: Study user training plans, Champions programs, and how to measure Tableau ROI using built-in usage analytics.

certificationCard.description: Tableau Consultants implement Tableau solutions and advise organizations on analytics strategy, dashboard design, and data visualization best practices.

keyConcepts.h2: Tableau Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Requirements and Solution Design
blocks.body: Tableau Consultants gather requirements by understanding: what business questions need answering, what data sources exist and their quality, who the end users are (executives vs analysts vs frontline), and how the dashboards will be maintained. A good solution design specifies: data source strategy (published vs embedded, live vs extract), visualisation types (matching the analytical question), and the deployment plan (who publishes, who maintains). The consultant also assesses data readiness — is the data structured appropriately for Tableau, or does it need preparation in Prep Builder first?

blocks.heading: Advanced Calculations: LOD Expressions
blocks.body: Level of Detail (LOD) expressions are Tableau's most powerful calculation type. FIXED: computes a value at a specific dimension level regardless of the view's level of detail — e.g., {'{'}FIXED [Region]: SUM([Sales]){'}'} gives sales per region in every row. INCLUDE: adds dimensions to the view LOD for the calculation. EXCLUDE: removes dimensions from the view LOD. Common use cases: cohort analysis, year-over-year comparison at a fixed level, customer-level metrics in transaction-level views. The exam tests which LOD expression type applies to a given analysis scenario.

blocks.heading: Dashboard Design Principles
blocks.body: Effective dashboard layout: use containers (horizontal and vertical) to control component resizing and alignment. Padding and spacing separate sections visually. Filter placement: global filters affect all sheets; local filters affect one. Dashboard actions (Filter Action, Highlight Action, URL Action, Set Action) create interactivity — clicking one chart filters another. Mobile layout optimization defines a separate layout for phone-size screens. The consultant also validates dashboard performance — too many filters, marks, or cross-database queries degrade user experience.

blocks.heading: Tableau Prep Builder: Data Preparation
blocks.body: Tableau Prep Builder creates Flow pipelines for data cleaning and reshaping before loading to Tableau Desktop or Server. Steps: Input (connect to source), Clean (remove nulls, fix data types, rename fields), Aggregate (roll up), Join (combine tables), Union (stack rows), Pivot (reshape wide to tall or vice versa), Output (Hyper extract, CSV, or Published Data Source). Flows can be published to Tableau Server/Cloud and scheduled for automated refresh. The consultant assesses whether source data requires Prep preprocessing before it can be visualised effectively.

blocks.heading: Tableau Server Administration for Consultants
blocks.body: Consultants configure Tableau Server for clients: create sites (for multi-tenancy — each site is isolated), configure projects and permissions, set up user authentication (Local, Active Directory, **SAML** **SSO**), and schedule extract refreshes. Subscriptions send emailed snapshots of views on a schedule. Webhooks trigger external systems when Tableau events occur (publish, refresh completion). The consultant advises on content governance — project structure, who can publish where, certification workflows, and data source governance to prevent fragmented analytics environments.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Tableau Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Tableau Consultant exam tests implementation and solution design skills for Tableau projects. Focus on discovery, solution architecture, performance best practices, and advising clients on Tableau deployment strategies.

blocks.heading: Discovery & Requirements
blocks.body: Know how to run a Tableau discovery: understanding existing data sources, report inventory, user personas, and governance requirements. Map business requirements to Tableau features and identify migration complexity.

blocks.heading: Solution Architecture Decisions
blocks.body: Know when to use Tableau Server vs. Tableau Cloud, Desktop vs. Prep, live vs. extract connections, and published data sources vs. embedded data. Justify each decision based on security, performance, and governance needs.

blocks.heading: Data Preparation Strategy
blocks.body: Know when to use Tableau Prep vs. database-side transformations vs. Tableau Desktop calculated fields. Understand the performance implications of each approach for large data volumes.

blocks.heading: User Adoption Strategy
blocks.body: Know how to drive Tableau adoption: training plans for different user personas, Tableau Champions programs, usage analytics, and how to measure ROI through Tableau's usage data.

blocks.heading: Performance Best Practices
blocks.body: Know how to advise clients on workbook performance: minimizing marks, using context filters effectively, optimizing data source queries, and using extracts to improve dashboard responsiveness.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the primary role of a Salesforce Certified Tableau Consultant?
options: Implementing Tableau solutions and advising on analytics best practices
sampleQuestions.explanation: Tableau Consultants implement Tableau solutions and advise stakeholders on analytics design, governance, and best practices.

sampleQuestions.question: Which skill is essential for a Tableau Consultant?
options: Requirements gathering, data modeling, visualization design, and stakeholder communication
sampleQuestions.explanation: Consultants need requirements gathering, data modeling, visualization design, and stakeholder communication skills.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the difference between dimensions and measures in Tableau?
options: Dimensions are categorical (blue pills); measures are numeric aggregations (green pills)
sampleQuestions.explanation: Dimensions create headers and categories; measures are aggregated. Understanding this is core to Tableau data modeling.

sampleQuestions.question: Which chart type is best for showing trends over time?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Line charts effectively show trends and patterns over continuous time.

sampleQuestions.question: What does LOD (Level of Detail) expression control in Tableau?
options: The granularity at which calculations are performed (FIXED, INCLUDE, EXCLUDE)
sampleQuestions.explanation: LOD expressions let you compute at a different granularity than the view level.

sampleQuestions.question: When should you use a Tableau extract versus a live connection?
options: Use extracts when you need faster performance and can refresh periodically; live when real-time data is critical
sampleQuestions.explanation: Extracts improve performance; live connections support real-time requirements. Consultants choose based on use case.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of Tableau's dual axis?
options: Plots two measures with different scales on the same axis for comparison
sampleQuestions.explanation: Dual axis lets you overlay two measures with different scales for comparison.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Tableau filter type applies before data is aggregated?
options: Extract filter and data source filter apply earliest; dimension filters before aggregation
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data source and extract filters run first; dimension filters apply before aggregation. Measure filters apply after.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Tableau parameter used for?
options: Letting users dynamically change values (e.g., top N, thresholds) that drive calculations and filters
sampleQuestions.explanation: Parameters allow interactive control over calculations, filters, and reference lines.

sampleQuestions.question: Which visualization best shows part-to-whole relationships?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Pie charts and treemaps show proportions of a whole. Consultants choose based on number of categories.

sampleQuestions.question: What does Tableau's 'Show Me' panel help with?
options: Recommending chart types based on selected fields and data types
sampleQuestions.explanation: Show Me suggests appropriate chart types based on the fields you select.

sampleQuestions.question: When gathering requirements for a dashboard, what should a consultant prioritize?
options: Key metrics, user roles, refresh frequency, and data sources
sampleQuestions.explanation: Requirements should cover metrics, users, refresh needs, and data sources to design effective solutions.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the benefit of calculated fields in Tableau?
options: They create new metrics and dimensions from existing data without changing the source
sampleQuestions.explanation: Calculated fields extend your data model for analysis without modifying source systems.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Tableau feature supports collaborative design and governance?
options: Tableau Server/Cloud with projects, permissions, and certified data sources
sampleQuestions.explanation: Tableau Server and Cloud enable projects, permissions, and certified content for team collaboration.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Tableau story used for?
options: Guiding viewers through a narrative using a sequence of dashboards and text
sampleQuestions.explanation: Stories combine worksheets and text to present a narrative and guide analysis.
